newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Ahold Q1 net strong on acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ahold Q1 net strong on acquisitions.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV on Thursday reported a 69 percent increase in 1997 first quarter net profit to 234.4 million guilders ($121 million), mainly thanks to acquisitions in the United States.
Repeating a forecast of considerably higher results in 1997, it said the sharp rise in net earnings was mainly attributable to last year's acquisition of U.S. supermarket chain Stop & Shop.
The figures and the forecast were broadly in line with analyst expectations, which had ranged from 227 to 255 million guilders.
"Nothing very surprising, overall, the outcome is fine, and so is the repeat of their forecast," said Jurgen Veenker, analyst at MeesPierson.
The stronger dollar -- valued at 1.87 guilders in the first quarter of 1997 versus 1.65 guilders in the same period of 1996 -- also had a positive impact on earnings and turnover.

First quarter sales rose 48 percent to 14.0 billion guilders. Ahold said the increase in first quarter sales would have been only 17 percent if Stop & Shop had also been included in consolidated sales figures for the first quarter of 1996.
The company said growth of operating results had been achieved in most of the company's operating regions, although Poland, Spain and in the Asia Pacific region continued to report start-up losses.

Ahold said the 144 percent increase in operating results to $159.1 million in the U.S. had been partially influenced by the operating results of Stop & Shop, but Ahold's other U.S. chains also performed well.
"BI-LO, Giant (including Edwards) and Tops (including Finast) also posted consideraly higher operating results," the company said.

Operating results in the Netherlands were up 9.8 percent to 165.5 million guilders, as supermarket store chain Albert Heijn, grocery wholesaler Schuitema and Ahold Institutional Food Supply posted higher profits.
Operating results at Ahold Specialty Stores and Ahold's Dutch production companies were slightly lower than last year.
Ahold operating income generated in other European countries was up two million guilders to 34.3 million.
Ahold said a notably higher operating result had been achieved in Portugal, whereas those in the Czech republic had been slightly lower.
Ahold achieved an operating income of 15.8 million guilders in Brazil, where it took a 50 percent stake in Brazilian supermarkets group Bompreco in December last year.
Bompreco has annual sales of some $1.4 billion.
Start-up costs for new activities in the Asia Pacific region led to an operating loss of 15 million guilders.
Ahold confirmed a previously announced three-for-one stock split would be effective July 21 of this year. It said the stock split would also apply to its ADRs traded in New York.
Ahold shares slightly dipped on the figures, touching a low of 154.30 guilders before bouncing back to 159.80 guilders for a 3.10 rise from Wednesday's closing level.
